title: The caste system in India
summary: One review calls the Indian caste system one of the oldest institutionalized forms of oppression, in existence for over 3,000 years. It combines two concepts: varna, the four orders of Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra in Hindu sacred texts, and jati. Dalits, at the bottom, face discrimination to this day. The review says the system was formalized during British colonial rule.

uncertainty.note: Textual foundations trace to the Rigveda and late Vedic period (c. 1500–500 BCE), with hereditary endogamous jati structures crystallizing in the mid-first millennium BCE and continuing until formal legal prohibition of discrimination in the 1950 Constitution of India.

as_recorded.value: Ancient India in the Vedic Period (c. 1500-1000 BCE) did not have social stratification based on socio-economic indicators; rather, citizens were classified according to their Varna or castes.
there can be only four varnas – that is, Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra
